_comment: Code-scanning alerts dismissed by .github/workflows/code-scanning.yml (contrib/secops/code-scanning-triage.py). One entry per tool + rule + path glob: reason is one of 'false positive', 'won't fix', 'used in tests'; comment is the argument a reviewer can check (280 characters reach GitHub). A real finding is fixed in code, never listed here.

dismissals.comment: The UIDs are the ones the images bake in (ycash6 contrib/docker/ycashd/Dockerfile:34 uid 2001; lightwalletd-dd 2002; images/yindex 2003, images/faucet 2004; redis 999, postgres 70, nginx 101). A change re-owns the PVC datadirs. Pods run non-root, no escalation, caps dropped.

CPU limits are off on purpose: CFS throttling stalls ycashd RPC, lightwalletd gRPC and yindex under bursts. Every container has a CPU request and a memory limit (values.yaml, values-kind.yaml, values-eks.yaml); the lightwalletd HPA scales on CPU.

No NetworkPolicy yet: the pods' ingress is the Envoy Gateway (its own namespace) and Prometheus, and enforcement depends on the CNI. Owner decision. Nothing in the cluster holds a key (AGENTS.md rule 4); node RPC needs rpcuser/rpcpassword.

Only the kind arming Job (templates/kind/arm.yaml) mounts a token: it runs kubectl to write the set ConfigMap/Secret and roll the node, with its own ServiceAccount and a namespace Role. Every other pod sets automountServiceAccountToken: false.

Only the kind miner (templates/kind/regtest.yaml) has none: a shell loop of `ycash-cli generate 1` with no port or health endpoint, retrying a failed generate itself. Every container with a port has a liveness probe.
Only the kind miner (templates/kind/regtest.yaml) has none: it serves nothing and has no port, so readiness has no meaning. Every serving container has a readiness probe.
aws_security_group.rds is attached: module "rds" sets vpc_security_group_ids = [aws_security_group.rds.id] (rds.tf). Checkov's graph does not follow the reference into the module.

Both values are generated by Terraform (random_password) and synced by External Secrets; Secrets Manager rotation needs a Lambda per secret that also re-keys ycashd or RDS. Rotation is `terraform apply -replace=random_password.<name>`. Owner decision.
The two secrets use the AWS-managed aws/secretsmanager key. A customer-managed KMS key adds a key, its policy and its monthly cost: an owner decision, not a silent change.

ECR uses AES256 (SSE-S3). encryption_configuration forces replacement: switching to KMS recreates the four repositories and drops their images. Owner decision; the images are builds of public source trees.

azs is the first three sorted zone names of var.region (main.tf module vpc). Pinning names needs a per-region list (us-west-1 has no 'a'), and a new zone does not move an applied VPC's subnets. A var.azs is the fix if wanted.
